evidence: Suet. Vesp. 16: coemendō quaedam tantum ut plūris posteā distraheret (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. sale: retail (mercēs distrahere)
terms.comment: In the language of trade, to sell off in separate lots (Lewis & Short, mostly post-Augustan); its first sense is to pull apart. Buying up in bulk is coemere.

evidence: Cic. Pis. 67: pānis et vīnum ā propōlā atque dē cūpā (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Greek προπώλης: the dealer who sells to the public, often with a hint of the huckster. In Cicero’s line Piso’s bread and wine come from the shop and the cask, not from his own stores.
Rare (Lewis & Short): of property or booty sold off in parcels rather than of shop trade.

phrases.english: This retailer sells everything at a higher price.

sources: Lewis & Short: distraho · Lewis & Short: propola · Lewis & Short: divendo · Lewis & Short: coemo
